name: Discount codes
needs: add a coupon code box to my checkout
give a launch discount for the first 100 customers
make a promo code for an influencer
summary: Codes customers type at checkout to get money off, and the rules behind them: how much, for how long, for whom, and how many times. Payment platforms keep the rules on their side, so a code can't be faked from the browser.
need_when: You're launching and want to reward early buyers.
You give creators or partners their own codes and want to see what each one brings in.
Your sales team gives some customers a special price.
skip_when: You don't plan to offer discounts. Then leave the code box off your checkout.

ways.title: Your payment platform's promo codes
ways.how: Create coupons and promotion codes in Stripe, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy and turn on the code field in their checkout. Stripe's allow_promotion_codes adds the box.
ways.tradeoff: Limits, expiry and first order rules are built in. You're tied to their checkout and their rules.

ways.title: Discounts applied by your server
ways.how: Your code decides who gets a deal and applies a coupon to their subscription or checkout, so the customer never types anything.
ways.tradeoff: Good for sales deals and win back offers. No shareable code, so it doesn't help with promotions.

ways.title: Your own discount table
ways.how: Store codes, amounts, expiry, use limits and redemptions in your database and work out the price yourself.
ways.tradeoff: Full control. Easy to get rounding, stacking and race conditions wrong, and the payment record has to match your math.

prompt:
Add discount codes to checkout.

Requirements:
- Use [Stripe promotion codes / Paddle discounts / Lemon Squeezy discounts]. Keep every rule on the payment platform or the server, never in the browser.
- Codes can be a percentage or a fixed amount, last [once / for N months / forever], expire on a date and have a total use limit.
- Support a first order only rule and codes tied to one customer.
- Show a clear message for codes that are wrong, expired or used up, and don't change the price.
- Save the code and the amount it took off on each order, so I can report sales per code.
- Two people using the last remaining use of a code at the same moment: only one gets it.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Enter a valid code at checkout. The total drops by the right amount before payment.
2. Enter an expired code, a used up code and a made up code. Each one is refused with a clear message and the price doesn't change.
3. A code limited to first orders is refused for a customer who has bought before.
4. The order or invoice shows which code was used and how much it took off.

if_you_skip_it: Launch deals and partner codes turn into manual refunds after the sale, and a code shared too widely can't be shut off or tracked.
